topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the lecture and outlines its focus on the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns in immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the microbial and cellular damage patterns that trigger innate immunity and establish the evolutionary criteria for distinguishing self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptors and downstream inflammatory signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genetics, subcellular localization, and downstream signaling cascades of key pattern recognition receptor families, including Toll-like receptors and cytosolic inflammasomes.

topics.label: Cellular mediation, leukocyte trafficking, and systemic inflammatory responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells coordinate the acute inflammatory cascade, orchestrate leukocyte recruitment and lymphatic priming, and risk triggering severe systemic complications like sepsis.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic adaptations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how acute inflammation is brought to a close, how tissue architecture is repaired, and how failed clearance leads to chronic inflammation or granuloma containment.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the complement system.
